_comment: What the demonstrator knows about ExpenseDesk period reports. Used as the scripted stand-in for a human when testing whether an induction can use a rule it is told. The first matching rule wins and nothing else is volunteered.

rules.answer: Different reasons, and they matter separately. clm_3005 and clm_3008 are not approved yet, so they are not spend. clm_3007 is approved but belongs to a different period. clm_3003 and clm_3006 are approved and in period, but meals and entertainment are reimbursed through a separate system and never appear in a period expense report.

Meals and entertainment are reimbursed through a separate system, so they are never included in a period expense report even when the claim is approved. That is why the dinner and the team coffee were left out.
A report covers exactly one period. An approved claim from another period is excluded, because it will have been reported in its own month.
Only approved claims are reimbursed. Drafts and claims still awaiting approval are not yet spend and are excluded.
A missing receipt does not remove a line from an approved claim. Receipts matter at approval time, not at reporting time.
Totals are grouped by the cost center recorded on the claim itself, not by the submitting user's own cost center.
